{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Coordinate subgradient minimization on product domains with an independent optimizer radius\par}\vspace{5pt}


\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{SO\_\allowbreak{}FO\_\allowbreak{}CS01\_\allowbreak{}product\_\allowbreak{}radius\_\allowbreak{}csg}



Single-objective optimization



A coherent scalar coordinate interface is studied uniformly over public product geometries. The optimizer-distance budget is independent of the domain diameter, and coordinatewise-motion algorithms form a separate view.



\textbf{Status.} Logarithmic gap; Bounds missing



\textbf{TASK tags.} solution concept: Objective minimization; task family: Single objective



\textbf{MODEL tags.} convexity: Convex; smoothness: Lipschitz



\textbf{ORACLE tags.} feedback quality: Exact; operation: Coordinate subgradient; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared; scalar derivative order: Scalar-function first derivative



\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} randomization: Private randomness allowed; restriction: No additional span restriction explicitly imposed



\textbf{OUTPUT tags.} postprocessing: Unqueried output explicitly allowed



\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} quantifier: Algorithm before instance



\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} budget: Fixed worst-case budget; measure: N coordinate subgradient



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}


Given a public compact product domain \AtlasInlineMath{D} and initial point \AtlasInlineMath{x_1\in D}, minimize a hidden convex function over \AtlasInlineMath{D}. The complexity is uniform over the permitted public geometries, with the algorithm selected after the geometry is known.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}


The public domain is
\AtlasMath{D=\prod_{i=1}^d[\ell_i,u_i],\qquad-\infty<\ell_i\le u_i<\infty.}
 Singleton factors are allowed. There is no bound on \AtlasInlineMath{\operatorname{diam}(D)/R_B}.



An instance is a finite convex Euclidean \AtlasInlineMath{G}-Lipschitz function \AtlasInlineMath{f:D\to\mathbb R} and one fixed Borel map \AtlasInlineMath{g:D\to\mathbb R^d} such that
\AtlasMath{f(z)\ge f(x)+\langle g(x),z-x\rangle,\quad\|g(x)\|_2\le G\qquad(x,z\in D).}
 At boundary points this supporting inequality is relative to \AtlasInlineMath{D}.



At least one constrained minimizer satisfies \AtlasInlineMath{\frac12\|x^\star-x_1\|_2^2\le R_B^2}. The radius \AtlasInlineMath{R_B} is independent of the size of the product domain. The pair \AtlasInlineMath{(f,g)} is fixed before the private seed is sampled.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}


One query chooses \AtlasInlineMath{(x,i)\in D\times\{1,\ldots,d\}} and returns only the exact scalar \AtlasInlineMath{g_i(x)}. All coordinates at a point arise from the same pre-fixed vector \AtlasInlineMath{g(x)}. No function values, active labels, full gradients, coordinate minimizers, or off-domain observations are supplied.



The public inputs are \AtlasInlineMath{d,G,R_B,\varepsilon,D,x_1}. Projection onto the known product domain and operations on public geometry are free.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}


Return any measurable feasible point \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat x\in D} determined by the transcript, including an unqueried point or an average of iterates.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}


The loss is \AtlasInlineMath{f(\widehat x)-\min_{z\in D}f(z)}. The requirement concerns worst-instance expected loss over the independent private seed.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}


Every scalar coordinate response costs one call. The query cap holds on every seed and every legal response history. Exact centroid and support computations on known models, arithmetic, and storage are uncharged; their computational runtime is not a charged resource.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Unrestricted coordinates / Expected loss}


Queries, stopping decisions, and the output are measurable functions of the preceding transcript and an instance-independent private random seed. The unknown instance is fixed before the seed is realized. No span, support, zero-respecting, or memory restriction is imposed.



Internal exact-real computation and storage using public inputs and received information are uncharged. The stated budget must hold on every execution path.




\AtlasMath{\forall(D,x_1)\ \exists A_{D,x_1}\ \forall(f,g):\mathbb E[f(\widehat x)-\min_Df]\le\varepsilon}




The policy family is chosen using the public geometry. Expected error is uniform over all admissible hidden coherent instances, with a pathwise scalar-query cap.



\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_worst\_case



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Coordinatewise motion / Expected loss}


Queries, stopping decisions, and the output are measurable functions of the preceding transcript and an instance-independent private random seed. The unknown instance is fixed before the seed is realized. No span, support, zero-respecting, or memory restriction is imposed.



Internal exact-real computation and storage using public inputs and received information are uncharged. The stated budget must hold on every execution path.



If a query is made, the first query point is \AtlasInlineMath{x_1}. Successive actual query points obey \AtlasInlineMath{X_{t+1}-X_t\in\operatorname{span}\{e_{I_t}\}}. The output may be any feasible function of the transcript; no prescribed stepsize formula or last-iterate restriction is imposed.




\AtlasMath{\forall(D,x_1)\ \exists A_{D,x_1}\ \forall(f,g):\mathbb E[f(\widehat x)-\min_Df]\le\varepsilon}




The same worst-geometry expected-error guarantee is required under the stated motion restriction.



\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_worst\_case



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}


\AtlasInlineMath{d}: Number of scalar subgradient coordinates \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}}.



\AtlasInlineMath{G}: Bound on the Euclidean norm of the coherent selected subgradient \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{G>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{R_B}: Independent optimizer-distance budget \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{R_B>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\|x^\star-x_1\|_2\le\sqrt2R_B} for some minimizer



\AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}: Expected objective-error target \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{D}: Public compact product domain \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{D=\prod_i[\ell_i,u_i]}, finite endpoints.



\AtlasInlineMath{x_1}: Public initial point \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{x_1\in D}.



\AtlasInlineMath{q}: Normalized inverse accuracy \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{q>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{q=GR_B/\varepsilon}



\AtlasInlineMath{d_0}: Universal lower-bound dimension threshold \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d_0\in\mathbb N}.



Universal threshold in Theorem thm:main; no numerical value is asserted.



\AtlasInlineMath{q_0}: Universal lower-bound inverse-accuracy threshold \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{q_0>=1}.



Universal threshold in Theorem thm:main; independent of d,G,R\_B and the geometry.
